newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares stay virtually flat, seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares stay virtually flat, seen easing.

text.p: Polish shares stayed virtually flat in higher turnover and analysts saw them easing on Thursday on the back of stronger selling after price fixing but said stabilisation was likely on Friday or next week.
The main market's WIG index eased 0.1 percent to 14,123.4, and turnover rose 9.3 percent to 112.6 million zlotys ($40.2 million) on both markets as 31 issues rose, 20 fell and 29 were flat.
Analysts said the WIG index, currently at 14,123.4 points, was unlikely to fall below 14,000 or 13,500 points.

"Some stock prices start looking attractive and investors are likely to take advantage of that and I don't see any fundamental reasons for further falls," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.

He pointed out that the firms showed good September earnings and the overall economic climate was positive, which justified some growth or at least an end of falls, which took the WIG 6.3 percent down from the October 9 high of 15,078.7.

But analysts said the case of the construction firm Espebepe, which said it could go bankrupt if it failed to clinch a debt-cutting deal with its creditors, could have a cooling effect on the market, which so far has been spared bankruptcies of listed stocks.
Espebepe, Wednesday's top loser, plunged 9.6 percent and analysts saw it extending its fall in the next few sessions.

Analysts said primary market's offerings such as Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) and poultry producer Drosed were draining funds away from the bourse and said a stronger rebound was possible after some of the capital flows back into the market in mid-November.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 3.8 percent in 32.7- million-zloty ($11.7 million) trade in regular session but fell 1.3 percent in 16-million-zloty ($5.7 million) live trade.
